attrs.label: Internal
attrs.description:
Authenticated party inside the enterprise — employees,
contractors, operations stakeholders. Authenticates via the
enterprise identity provider; sees internal applications.

attrs.label: External
attrs.description:
Unauthenticated or partner_trust party outside the enterprise.
Reaches the system only through public surfaces (public_api,
partner_integration_endpoint, public_mcp_server).

attrs.label: External AI Agent
attrs.description:
Autonomous agent operated by a third party that interacts with
the enterprise via published machine surfaces (public_mcp_server,
partner_integration_endpoint). Distinct from `external` because
the semantics of agent_driven traffic differ — different rate
limits, different audit trails, different consent model. Worth a
separate visual treatment so a viewer can tell at a glance which
actors are humans vs which are agents.

attrs.label: Controller
attrs.description:
Handles inbound requests or events. The entry point from
outside the container.

attrs.label: Service
attrs.description: Orchestrates business logic within the container.

attrs.label: Repository
attrs.description:
Encapsulates data access; mediates between domain logic
and the underlying store.

attrs.label: Adapter
attrs.description:
Translates between the container's internal model and an
external system or protocol.

attrs.label: Validator
attrs.description:
Enforces rules and invariants; rejects malformed or
non_compliant inputs.

attrs.label: Mapper
attrs.description: Translates between data shapes — DTO, entity, view_model.

attrs.label: Client
attrs.description:
Outbound call to another container or external system.
The complement to a controller.

attrs.label: Business Product
attrs.description:
123
                A named, business_funded software product owned end_to_end
                by a product team or cost centre. Typically contains other
                applications and/or has its own containers; rarely provides
                components directly. The thing the business funds and
                reports on.

attrs.label: Vendor Installation
attrs.description:
A specific deployed instance of a procured product — our
Salesforce tenant, our particular Power Platform environment,
our SAP S/4 installation. Distinct from the vendor's product
as a market offering (that's a `technology`). May provide
multiple `component`s representing capabilities the tenant
offers.

attrs.label: Internal Service
attrs.description:
An implementation_level deployable unit owned by an
engineering team — the order_events service, the
customer_master service. Typically provides exactly one
`component` (itself) and may consume many. Often wears both
hats: component (capability slot) plus application
(identity).

attrs.label: Portfolio
attrs.description:
A composite that aggregates multiple applications for
governance and reporting — e.g., a Sales Experience that
wraps several underlying products. Only contains; rarely
has direct containers.

attrs.label: Planned
attrs.description: Approved or proposed; not yet built or operational.

attrs.label: Live
attrs.description: Operational and supported in production.

attrs.label: Sunset
attrs.description:
Operational but being phased out; new dependencies should
be discouraged. Replacement (if any) is declared via the
app_to_app replacement relationship in a follow_up.

attrs.label: Retired
attrs.description:
No longer operational. Kept in the model for historical
accuracy and to anchor `replaces` relationships from
successor applications.

attrs.label: M365 Copilot USL
attrs.description:
Absorbed by the Microsoft 365 Copilot user
subscription licence under fair_use limits. Applies
to components that run under the authenticated M365
Copilot_licensed user's identity — typically the
M365 Copilot orchestrator and skills it invokes
inline.

attrs.label: Copilot Credits
attrs.description:
Metered against the tenant's Microsoft Copilot
Studio Copilot Credit pool (prepaid pack or
pay_as_you_go meter). Applies to Copilot Studio
orchestrator dispatches, agent actions, generative
answers, tenant_graph grounding, and autonomous
agent runs outside the M365 Copilot umbrella.

attrs.label: Azure Consumption
attrs.description:
Direct Azure resource consumption — SKU_based or
per_unit (tokens, requests, throughput units).
Applies to Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Search, App
Service / Functions, Service Bus, Event Hubs, and
similar infrastructure components whose meters are
billed against the Azure subscription, not against
a Copilot licence.

attrs.label: Web Portal
attrs.description: Browser-rendered application accessed via URL.

attrs.label: Mobile App
attrs.description: Native or hybrid mobile application.

attrs.label: Desktop App
attrs.description: Native desktop application installed on a workstation.

attrs.label: Conversational Interface
attrs.description: Chat-based front-end through which actors converse with the system.

attrs.label: Legacy Application
attrs.description: Pre-existing application not slated for replacement; integrated via adapters.

attrs.label: Embedded Widget
attrs.description: Application surface hosted inside another application's chrome.

attrs.label: Reporting Surface
attrs.description: Dashboard or report-rendering application.

attrs.label: Forms Solution
attrs.description: Tool for authoring forms, surveys, and quizzes with response collection and analytics.

attrs.label: Scheduling Solution
attrs.description: Application for managing customer appointments, calendar coordination, and meeting bookings.

attrs.label: Video Editing Solution
attrs.description: Application for recording, editing, and publishing video content.

attrs.label: Virtual Desktop Infrastructure
attrs.description: Cloud-hosted desktop and application virtualisation; users connect to remote sessions instead of local installs.

attrs.label: Email Solution
attrs.description: Hosted email and calendaring platform providing mailboxes, distribution lists, and shared calendars.

attrs.label: SMB ERP Solution
attrs.description: ERP application targeted at small and mid-sized businesses, bundling finance, sales, service, and operations.

attrs.label: Enterprise ERP Solution
attrs.description: ERP application targeted at large enterprises, covering finance, supply chain, manufacturing, HR, or commerce at scale; per-module configuration and operational-system integration are typical.

attrs.label: Enterprise Feedback Management Solution
attrs.description: Application for collecting customer or employee feedback at scale through surveys, with response orchestration and insights integrated with downstream CRM/HR systems.

attrs.label: API Service
attrs.description: A service that exposes a programmatic interface; typically RESTful or RPC.

attrs.label: Workflow Engine
attrs.description: Orchestrates long-running processes spanning multiple services or human steps.

attrs.label: Orchestration Engine
attrs.description: Coordinates short-running interactions between agents or services.

attrs.label: Microservices Runtime
attrs.description: Managed runtime for stateful and stateless microservices, distinct from Kubernetes container orchestration.

attrs.label: Integration Adapter
attrs.description: Bridges between architectures or between protocols/data formats.

attrs.label: Event Processor
attrs.description: Consumes events from a stream and reacts (transform, dispatch, accumulate).

attrs.label: Notification Service
attrs.description: Delivers messages to actors via email, push, SMS, etc.

attrs.label: AI Agent
attrs.description: An autonomous or semi-autonomous AI workload that takes actions on behalf of a user or system.

attrs.label: Language Model
attrs.description: Foundation model serving completions/embeddings.

attrs.label: RAG
attrs.description: Retrieval-augmented generation pipeline component.

attrs.label: Scheduler
attrs.description: Triggers workloads on a time- or event-based schedule.

attrs.label: Authorization Service
attrs.description: Decides whether a principal may perform an action on a resource.

attrs.label: Platform API
attrs.description: A unified platform-wide programmatic surface (e.g. Microsoft Graph).

attrs.label: Relational Store
attrs.description: Tables-and-rows persistence.

attrs.label: Document Store
attrs.description: Semi-structured document persistence.

attrs.label: File Store
attrs.description: Blob/object storage indexed by path or key.

attrs.label: Archive Store
attrs.description: Cold-tier storage for rarely-accessed data with long retention; retrieval may be deferred.

attrs.label: Configuration Store
attrs.description: Managed store for application settings and feature flags shared across services.

attrs.label: Event Log
attrs.description: Append-only stream of events; consumers replay or tail.

attrs.label: Message Queue
attrs.description: Point-to-point durable message delivery.

attrs.label: Knowledge Source
attrs.description: External or curated body of knowledge intended for AI grounding.

attrs.label: Analytical Store
attrs.description: Columnar / OLAP store optimised for aggregate queries.

attrs.label: Cache
attrs.description: In-memory or near-memory store for fast retrieval.

attrs.label: Internal API Gateway
attrs.description: Aggregates and exposes internal APIs to in-tenant consumers.

attrs.label: Message Topic
attrs.description: Pub/sub topic exposing event streams across capabilities.

attrs.label: Internal MCP Server
attrs.description: Model Context Protocol server exposing tools to in-tenant agents.

attrs.label: Public API
attrs.description: API exposed across the enterprise trust boundary.

attrs.label: Partner Integration Endpoint
attrs.description: B2B integration surface for named external partners.

attrs.label: Public MCP Server
attrs.description: Model Context Protocol server exposed to external agents.

attrs.label: Enterprise API Catalogue
attrs.description: Discoverable registry of APIs across the enterprise.

attrs.label: Federated Identity Provider
attrs.description: Identity provider trusted across capability boundaries.

attrs.label: Non-Human Identity Provider
attrs.description: Identity provider issuing credentials to agents, workloads, and service principals (as opposed to end users).

attrs.label: Domain Services
attrs.description: Managed directory providing classic Active Directory features (domain join, group policy, LDAP, Kerberos) without on-prem domain controllers.

attrs.label: Semantic Index
attrs.description: Cross-capability vector / semantic search index.

attrs.label: Secret Store
attrs.description: Managed store for secrets, keys, and certificates.

attrs.label: Hardware Security Module
attrs.description: FIPS-validated hardware for cryptographic key custody.

attrs.label: SIEM
attrs.description: Security information and event management; correlation, detection, and threat hunting.

attrs.label: Identity Threat Detection
attrs.description: Risk-based detection of compromised identities via sign-in and behaviour signals.

attrs.label: Cloud Security Posture Management
attrs.description: Continuous posture, compliance, and misconfiguration detection across cloud assets.

attrs.label: External Attack Surface Management
attrs.description: Discovers and monitors externally-exposed assets for risk.

attrs.label: IoT Security Monitor
attrs.description: Threat detection for OT/IoT devices and networks.

attrs.label: Data Protection Service
attrs.description: Information classification, labelling, and data loss prevention.

attrs.label: Confidential Ledger
attrs.description: Tamper-evident, append-only ledger with cryptographic verification.

attrs.label: Virtual Network
attrs.description: Tenant-scoped software-defined network.

attrs.label: Global Network Backbone
attrs.description: Provider-managed global WAN / SD-WAN backbone.

attrs.label: NAT Gateway
attrs.description: Managed network address translation for egress traffic.

attrs.label: Private Endpoint Service
attrs.description: Private network endpoints into managed cloud services.

attrs.label: Dedicated Network Circuit
attrs.description: Dedicated physical or virtual circuit between on-prem and cloud.

attrs.label: VPN Gateway
attrs.description: IPsec/SSL VPN gateway bridging external networks.

attrs.label: Zero Trust Network Access
attrs.description: Identity-brokered per-app access to private resources without a full-tunnel VPN.

attrs.label: Network Firewall
attrs.description: L3/L4 network firewall with policy-based filtering.

attrs.label: Web Application Firewall
attrs.description: L7 HTTP/HTTPS request filtering for web applications.

attrs.label: Secure Web Gateway
attrs.description: Cloud-delivered egress filtering, URL/category controls, and internet access policy for identities (part of SSE/SASE).

attrs.label: DDoS Protection
attrs.description: Volumetric and protocol attack mitigation.

attrs.label: Load Balancer
attrs.description: L4 traffic distribution across backends.

attrs.label: DNS Service
attrs.description: Authoritative or recursive DNS resolution.

attrs.label: CDN / Edge
attrs.description: Global edge network with content delivery, caching, and public-facing routing.

attrs.label: Container Registry
attrs.description: OCI/Docker image and artifact registry.

attrs.label: Container Service

attrs.label: Kubernetes Platform

attrs.label: Container Persistent Volume Service

attrs.label: IoT Edge Runtime

attrs.label: Private Cloud Appliance

attrs.label: Edge Kubernetes Distribution

attrs.label: Network Function Manager

attrs.label: HPC Cluster Manager

attrs.label: Virtual Machine

attrs.label: Batch Compute

attrs.label: Static Web App Hosting

attrs.label: Quantum Compute Service

attrs.label: Streaming Analytics

attrs.label: Digital Twin Store

attrs.label: Knowledge Graph

attrs.label: ML Lifecycle Platform

attrs.label: Lakehouse Platform

attrs.label: Big Data Analytics Platform

attrs.label: Observability Dashboard

attrs.label: Cloud Health Feed

attrs.label: Cloud Advisory Service

attrs.label: Policy Engine
attrs.description: Authors and enforces governance policy at the control plane.

attrs.label: Cost Management Service
attrs.description: Cost visibility, budgets, and chargeback.

attrs.label: Cloud Control Plane

attrs.label: IaC Template Engine
attrs.description: Declarative templates for cloud resource provisioning.

attrs.label: Backup Service

attrs.label: Disaster Recovery Service

attrs.label: Chaos Engineering

attrs.label: Geospatial Service

attrs.label: IoT Platform Suite
attrs.description: Umbrella IoT product spanning device management, ingestion, and analytics.

attrs.label: Secured Microcontroller Platform
attrs.description: Hardware-rooted secured microcontroller with OS and cloud service.

attrs.label: Embedded IoT OS
attrs.description: Embedded operating system for IoT devices.

attrs.label: VNet Peering
attrs.description:
Azure_style vnet peering — routed private link between
two vnets in the same or different regions. AWS VPC
peering and GCP VPC Network Peering belong here too.

attrs.label: ExpressRoute
attrs.description:
Dedicated private circuit between a cloud vnet and an
on_premises network. Carries the BGP_routed traffic
via a customer_owned edge router; no public internet
transit.

attrs.label: Site-to-Site VPN
attrs.description:
IPSec_tunnelled link between a vnet and an on_premises
network. Lower bandwidth than ExpressRoute; uses public
internet as transport but encrypts the payload.

attrs.label: Point-to-Site VPN
attrs.description:
Per_device VPN client connecting a single host (user
laptop, admin jumpbox) to a vnet. Less common in
architecture_level modelling; included for completeness.

attrs.label: Calls
attrs.description:
Synchronous runtime invocation. A calls B and waits for response.
Default for scenario steps when no kind is annotated; the most
common edge in any architecture.

attrs.label: Event
attrs.description:
Asynchronous runtime emission. A emits an event B reacts to.
Visual rendering and semantics differ from `calls` (UML's
async_message convention is what we follow here). When the
receiver is a topic/queue/log, prefer this over `calls` even if
the wire_level mechanics involve a synchronous publish API.

attrs.label: Consumes
attrs.description:
A reads or uses data/services from B as part of its operation.
Distinct from `calls` (no specific method invocation; can be
data flow, subscription, lookup). Common targets: data stores,
knowledge sources, semantic indexes.

attrs.label: Available Through
attrs.description:
A is exposed/accessed via B. The "access path" relationship —
a public API exposed through an internal gateway, a tool exposed
through an MCP server, a model served through an inference
endpoint.

attrs.label: Enabled By
attrs.description:
B is the platform/tool used to author, build, or configure A.
Build_time / authoring relationship. Example: a Power Platform
agent is enabled_by Copilot Studio (the authoring surface), not
hosted_by it.

attrs.label: Hosted By
attrs.description:
B is the runtime container that operates A in production. UML's
`«deploy»` stereotype. Distinct from enabled_by because the same
tool may both author AND host an artifact (Copilot Studio does
both for its agents) — the model says so explicitly with two
separate hosted_by + enabled_by edges.

attrs.label: Integration
attrs.description:
Peer_to_peer data or control exchange between two
applications. The typical app_to_app connector —
sales_console integrates with customer_360,
agent_bridge integrates with agent_service.

attrs.label: Replacement
attrs.description:
Lifecycle transition between two applications.
Application A is being replaced by application B;
renders as a transition arrow in app_portfolio and
modernization views. Both apps continue to compile —
the connector records the intent, not a hard cut_over.
Desugared from the `==>` operator.

attrs.label: Runtime Dependency
attrs.description:
A depends on B being available at runtime without a
direct data/control integration — shared identity,
shared infrastructure, environmental prerequisite.
Distinguishes 'integrates with' from 'requires the
presence of'. Desugared from the `~~>` operator.

attrs.label: Web Tier
attrs.description:
User_facing web, mobile, or desktop UX. The presentation
surface that actors interact with directly.

attrs.label: Service Tier
attrs.description:
Backend service or API; orchestrates business logic between
presentation and persistence.

attrs.label: Data Tier
attrs.description:
Container that holds state — database, document store,
table set, blob store. The container is the data, not
just an accessor of it.

attrs.label: Integration Tier
attrs.description:
Adapter or connector to external systems. Bridges to
vendor products, partner integrations, or legacy
applications.

attrs.label: Batch Tier
attrs.description:
Scheduled or asynchronous processing. Long_running jobs,
ETL pipelines, queue consumers.

attrs.label: Gateway Tier
attrs.description:
API gateway, reverse proxy, or backend_for_frontend.
Aggregates upstream services for downstream presentation.

attrs.label: Messaging Tier
attrs.description:
Message bus or event broker owned by the application
(not the shared platform). Pub/sub, queues, event streams.

attrs.label: Cross-Cutting
attrs.description:
Observability, configuration, security wrapper, or other
capability that doesn't sit on the main result_production
chain.

attrs.label: Power Platform Managed Environment
attrs.description:
A Power Platform environment with Managed Environments
features enabled. May or may not have VNet integration
(subnet injection via enterprise policy).

attrs.label: Power Platform Classic Environment
attrs.description:
A Power Platform environment without Managed Environments
features. Cannot have VNet integration; lives only in
Microsoft_managed M365 tenant infrastructure.

attrs.label: Azure Subscription Environment
attrs.description:
An Azure subscription serving as a deployment environment.
Either the subscription itself is the env (Pattern A:
env_per_sub) or a portion of the subscription (Pattern B/C:
env_scoped_to_RGs_within_sub).

attrs.label: AWS Account Environment
attrs.description:
An AWS account serving as a deployment environment.
Most common AWS pattern (one account per lifecycle).

attrs.label: On-Premises Deployment Group
attrs.description:
A logical grouping of on_premises deployments. May represent
a datacenter, a logical zone within a datacenter, or any
customer_defined on_prem deployment boundary.

attrs.label: Public Internet
attrs.description:
Slot accepts traffic from anywhere on the public internet.
Typically fronted by an API gateway, WAF, or load balancer
in a real deployment; the model captures the exposure
intent without committing to the specific edge device.

attrs.label: Private Endpoint
attrs.description:
Slot is reachable via private endpoint(s) from external
customer or partner networks. The endpoint pinning lives
on the network/subnet side; this value marks the slot as
accepting cross_organisation private traffic.

attrs.label: Development
attrs.description: Engineering team's working environment; not for end users.

attrs.label: Test
attrs.description: Integration / system test environment.

attrs.label: Staging
attrs.description:
Production_mirror environment for final validation before
release. Sometimes called pre_prod or UAT.

attrs.label: Production
attrs.description: Live production environment serving end users.

attrs.label: Sandbox
attrs.description:
Isolated environment for experimentation, demos, or training.
Not part of the standard delivery pipeline.

attrs.label: Cloud
attrs.description: Hosted in a public or private cloud (Azure, AWS, GCP).

attrs.label: PaaS
attrs.description: Platform-as-a-Service tier (App Service, ECS, Cloud Run).

attrs.label: SaaS
attrs.description: Software-as-a-Service tier (M365, Salesforce, Power Platform).

attrs.label: IaaS
attrs.description: Infrastructure-as-a-Service tier (raw VMs, networking).

attrs.label: Physical
attrs.description: Physical datacenter or hardware under enterprise control.

attrs.label: On-Premises
attrs.description: Customer-managed datacenter; typically `physical | on-premises`.

attrs.label: Logical
attrs.description: Organisational rollup with no hosting implication. Valid alone (e.g. "3rd-Party SaaS") or combined with a hosting flag.

attrs.label: Shared Network
attrs.description:
A network shared across multiple application teams or
workloads. Typical for a customer's enterprise vnet/VPC
that hosts many subnets serving different purposes.

attrs.label: Dedicated Network
attrs.description:
A network owned by a single application or workload. No
other team or workload deploys into it.

attrs.label: Hub Network
attrs.description:
The central network in a hub_and_spoke topology. Typically
hosts shared services (DNS, firewall, ExpressRoute
gateway) and peers to multiple spoke networks.

attrs.label: Spoke Network
attrs.description:
A workload network in a hub_and_spoke topology. Peers to
exactly one hub; reaches other spokes only via the hub.

attrs.label: On-Premises Segment
attrs.description:
A physical or logical network segment in the customer's
own datacenter, reachable from the cloud only via
ExpressRoute or VPN.

attrs.label: SaaS Vendor Fabric
attrs.description:
A vendor_managed network the customer doesn't control —
placeholder for the rare case where a network reference
is structurally needed but no real authoring detail
applies.
